newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares mixed, seen locked in tight range.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares mixed, seen locked in tight range.

text.p: Polish shares were mixed on Tuesday and analysts said the market was consolidating after recent gains and could see its next signal in the lower house of parliament's possible vote this week on 1997 taxes.
The lower house has said it might vote on Thursday on the Senate's amendments to 1997's tax bill which removed the lower house's steep tax cuts for low earners, seen as inflationary.
"I don't see any big movements up or down in the wait until Thursday," said Artur Czerwonski of Bank Pekao SA brokerage, noting the market's rise after the Senate's vote last week.
The main market's all-share WIG index rose 0.4 percent to 13,671.0 points and turnover rose 22.4 percent to 84.4 million zlotys on both markets.
Analysts said the stronger selling after price-fixing signalled a possible slight drop on Wednesday.
Others were heartened by the higher turnover and Tuesday's news industrial production was up 7.5 percent in October, 13.9 percent year-on-year against 14.1 percent in 1995.
"It shows production is comparable to last year, which should be a good longer-term signal" said Bogdan Kornacki, a trader at Wielkopolski Bank Kredytowy (WBK) brokerage.
Analysts said top gainer Swarzedz surged the daily maximum 10 percent after it recorded a net profit in October after a previously poor 1996.
Biggest loser Espebepe dropped 8.8 percent after its economic woes continued in October, with the firm losing 3.1 million zlotys on the month and 19.6 million this year.
Continuous trade turnover was at 1.7 million zlotys with three stocks down, one up and four flat.
NFI units rose 4.2 percent in the regular bourse session and were flat in 32.1-million-zloty continuous trade.
